description: What this shows: Signals derived from xrpld's debug.log via Loki (LogQL), covering detail that no metric or span records — manifest dispositions per master key, resource fee charges per IP and public key, ledger-fetch duplicate ratios, peer disconnect reasons, and consensus phase transitions.  —  Use it to: Investigate behaviour that the Prometheus dashboards cannot express, and to attribute load or abuse to a specific peer, key, or job.  —  REQUIRES DEBUG LOGS: most panels here read from log lines emitted at DBG severity, which xrpld suppresses by default (default threshold is Info, see Main.cpp). On a default-configured node those panels are EMPTY, and an empty panel here means 'not collecting', NOT 'no problem'. Enable per partition with `log_level <Partition> debug` — for example `log_level ManifestCache debug`. Rows are marked [DBG] when they require debug logs and [DEFAULT OK] when they work at the default Info level.

panels.title: Read This First — Debug Log Requirement

options.content:
### ⚠️ Most panels on this dashboard require debug logs

xrpld's default log threshold is **Info** (`Severity thresh = Severity::Info` in `Main.cpp`). Every panel in a row marked **[DBG]** reads log lines emitted at `DBG` severity, which a default-configured node **does not write**.

**An empty [DBG] panel means "not collecting", NOT "no problem".** A manifest dashboard reading zero because `ManifestCache` sits at Info is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

Enable per partition rather than globally — global debug is a firehose (`Resource` alone emits ~329k lines / 6h):

```
log_level ManifestCache debug
log_level Resource debug
log_level InboundLedger debug
log_level Peer debug
log_level LedgerConsensus debug
```

Rows marked **[DEFAULT OK]** work at the default Info level and need no configuration change.

panels.title: Nodes By Error Volume
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Which nodes are logging the most errors.*

###### How it's computed:
*Count of ERR and FTL log lines per node over the dashboard window, ranked highest first.*

###### Reading it:
*The top entry is the node in the most trouble. Compare nodes rather than reading an absolute value.*

###### Healthy range:
*Zero, or a small flat count. ERR is not routine.*

###### Watch for:
*Any node pulling far ahead of its peers, which usually means a fault local to that node rather than a network condition.*

###### Keywords:
- **ERR / FTL** *(per line)* — the two most severe xrpld log levels; both survive the default Info threshold.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a count over the dashboard window, ranked worst-first.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query by regex over raw log text.*

###### Source:
[Log.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/basics/Log.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logs::Sink::write`

###### References:
[Loki log queries](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/log_queries/)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (service_instance_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity =~ `ERR|FTL` [$__range])))

panels.title: Nodes By Attack-Like Input
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Which nodes are receiving the most malformed or unwanted peer payloads.*

###### How it's computed:
*Count of Resource fee charges whose reason is useless data, unwanted data, or init drop, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*These three reasons indicate a peer sent something the node could not use, so a high count is the closest log-derived proxy for abusive input.*

###### Healthy range:
*Low and flat. Some useless data is normal on a busy overlay.*

###### Watch for:
*A sharp rise on one node, especially paired with a single dominant IP in the charged-peers table below.*

###### Keywords:
- **Useless data** *(per charge)* — payload the node could not use, e.g. an empty or malformed message.
- **Init drop** *(per charge)* — a connection dropped during initialisation.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a count over the dashboard window, ranked worst-first.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query by regex over raw log text.*

###### Source:
[ResourceManager.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/resource/detail/ResourceManager.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logic::charge`

###### Note:
*Requires debug logs on the Resource partition.*

###### References:
[Peer protocol](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/peer-protocol)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (service_instance_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `Resource` |~ `useless data|unwanted data|init drop` [$__range])))

panels.title: Nodes By Total Fee Charged
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Which nodes are absorbing the most peer-imposed load, weighted by fee amount.*

###### How it's computed:
*Sum of every resource fee amount parsed from the Resource partition, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Weighted by cost rather than event count, so one heavy request at 2000 outranks eight moderate ones at 250.*

###### Healthy range:
*Proportional to peer count and request volume; compare nodes of similar role.*

###### Watch for:
*One node far above peers of the same role, which means it is carrying disproportionate peer load.*

###### Keywords:
- **Fee weight** *(per charge)* — the credit amount: 2000 heavy, 250 moderate, 150 useless data.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a count over the dashboard window, ranked worst-first.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query by regex over raw log text.*

###### Source:
[ResourceManager.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/resource/detail/ResourceManager.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logic::charge`

###### Note:
*Requires debug logs on the Resource partition.*

###### References:
[Peer protocol](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/peer-protocol)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `Resource` | regexp `\(\$(?P<fee>[0-9]+)\)` | unwrap fee [$__range])))

panels.title: Nodes By Manifest Rejection
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Which nodes are rejecting the most inbound manifests.*

###### How it's computed:
*Count of ManifestCache lines with a Stale, Invalid, Revoked, or UntrustedCapacity outcome, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A manifest flood shows up here first. Stale dominates normally because peers re-gossip manifests the node already holds.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; nodes on the same network should sit close together.*

###### Watch for:
*A single node far ahead, or any Invalid at all, which means a signature failed verification.*

###### Keywords:
- **Rejection** *(per manifest)* — any non-accepted disposition.
- **UntrustedCapacity** *(per manifest)* — rate-limit rejection for an unlisted key; rc5+ builds only.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a count over the dashboard window, ranked worst-first.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query by regex over raw log text.*

###### Source:
[Manifest.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/server/Manifest.cpp)

###### Function:
`ManifestCache::applyManifest`

###### Note:
*Requires debug logs on the ManifestCache partition.*

###### References:
[Validator keys](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/validator-keys)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (service_instance_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `ManifestCache` |~ `Manifest: (Stale|Invalid|Revoked|UntrustedCapacity)` [$__range])))

panels.title: Nodes By Consensus Problem
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Which nodes are logging the most consensus warnings and errors.*

###### How it's computed:
*Count of LedgerConsensus lines at WRN severity or above, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*Consensus is a network-wide process, so a single node standing out points at that node rather than the network.*

###### Healthy range:
*Low. Some warnings occur during normal round churn.*

###### Watch for:
*One node far above its peers, or a step change after a deploy.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus round** *(per ledger)* — one Open to Establish to Accepted cycle.
- **Dispute** *(per transaction)* — a transaction peers disagree about including.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a count over the dashboard window, ranked worst-first.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query by regex over raw log text.*

###### Source:
[Consensus.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/include/xrpl/consensus/Consensus.h)

###### Function:
`Consensus::timerEntry / checkConsensus`

###### References:
[Consensus](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (service_instance_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `LedgerConsensus` | severity =~ `WRN|ERR|FTL` [$__range])))

panels.title: Nodes By Job Latency Breach
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Which nodes are missing job latency targets most often.*

###### How it's computed:
*Count of LoadMonitor slow-job lines per node; the emitter only fires above a 500ms threshold.*

###### Reading it:
*A direct read on which node is most overloaded. Works at the default log level.*

###### Healthy range:
*Low. A busy node breaches occasionally.*

###### Watch for:
*A node far ahead of its peers, which usually means disk or CPU pressure local to it.*

###### Keywords:
- **Breach** *(per job)* — one job execution over the 500ms LoadMonitor threshold.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a count of BREACHES, never of total job executions.*
*Derived in the Grafana query. Use the native `job_*` metrics for totals.*

###### Source:
[LoadMonitor.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/LoadMonitor.cpp)

###### Function:
`LoadMonitor::addLoadSample`

###### Note:
*Counts breaches above 500ms only, so it is an exception count and not a latency measure.*

###### References:
[Job queue](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/JobQueue.cpp)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (service_instance_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `LoadMonitor` |~ `Job: .* run: [0-9]+ms wait: [0-9]+ms` [$__range])))

panels.title: Nodes By Sync Instability
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Which nodes are spending the most time out of the full state.*

###### How it's computed:
*Count of STATE-> transitions into any non-full state, per node.*

###### Reading it:
*A stable node holds full and emits nothing here, so any non-zero value means it left full that many times.*

###### Healthy range:
*Zero on a synced node.*

###### Watch for:
*A repeating count, which means the node is flapping rather than having had one bad moment.*

###### Keywords:
- **Operating mode** *(per node)* — Disconnected, Connected, Syncing, Tracking, Full.
- **Flapping** *(per node)* — repeated departures from full.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a count over the dashboard window, ranked worst-first.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query by regex over raw log text.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`NetworkOPsImp::setMode`

###### References:
[Server states](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/rippled-server-states)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (service_instance_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" |~ `STATE->(syncing|connected|tracking|disconnected)` [$__range])))

panels.title: Nodes By Duplicate Ledger Fetches
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Which nodes wasted the most ledger-fetch bandwidth, counted as duplicate SHAMap nodes received.*

###### How it's computed:
*Sum of the `dupe` counter from `Ledger AS/TX node stats` log lines, per node, over the dashboard window. `dupe` is matched by its own regex because the emitter omits any counter that is zero.*

###### Reading it:
*Every duplicate is a ledger node the peer sent that this node already held: bytes crossed the network, the peer spent resource credit serving it, and it was discarded.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent. Compare nodes of the same role rather than reading an absolute value; some duplication is unavoidable when fetching one ledger from several peers.*

###### Watch for:
*A node far ahead of its siblings, which points at that node's fetch logic or peer set rather than a network condition.*

###### Keywords:
- **Ledger node** *(per fetch)* — one SHAMap node fetched while acquiring a ledger.
- **Duplicate** *(per fetch)* — a node already held locally; wasted bandwidth and peer credit.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a COUNT of duplicates, not a ratio.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query via `unwrap` over raw log text.*

###### Source:
[InboundLedger.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/ledger/detail/InboundLedger.cpp)

###### Function:
`InboundLedger::onTimer`

###### Note:
*Requires debug logs on the InboundLedger partition. For the duplicate RATIO see "Ledger Node Fetch Duplicate Ratio" in the Ledger Acquisition Efficiency row — a stat panel cannot render a division, because Loki does not name binary-operation frames and Grafana falls back to "Value #A".*

###### References:
[Ledgers](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `InboundLedger` | regexp `dupe:(?P<dupe>[0-9]+)` | unwrap dupe [$__range])))

panels.title: Node State Transition Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of node operating-state transitions: disconnected, connected, syncing, tracking, and full.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of `STATE->` log lines, with the target state parsed from the line.*

###### Reading it:
*Each line is one transition INTO that state. A stable node sits in full and emits nothing.*

###### Healthy range:
*Flat at zero once synced. Any non-zero value means the node is changing state.*

###### Watch for:
*A repeating full to syncing to tracking to full cycle, which means the node cannot hold sync. Live observation shows 110 transitions per state per day on a flapping node.*

###### Keywords:
- **Operating mode / server state** *(per node)* — the node's sync level: Disconnected, Connected, Syncing, Tracking, Full.
- **Transition** *(per node)* — one `STATE->` log line, emitted only when the state actually changes.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series counts one server's own transitions.*
*NOT recorded as a metric anywhere. Derived entirely in the Grafana query by regex over raw log text; xrpld only writes the line.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`NetworkOPsImp::setMode`

###### References:
[Server states](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/rippled-server-states)

targets.expr: sum by (state, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `STATE->(?P<state>\w+)` | state != `` | label_format state=`{{if eq .state "full"}}Full{{else if eq .state "syncing"}}Syncing{{else if eq .state "tracking"}}Tracking{{else if eq .state "connected"}}Connected{{else if eq .state "disconnected"}}Disconnected{{else}}{{.state}}{{end}}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Node State Timeline
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The node's operating state over time, as a discrete timeline.*

###### How it's computed:
*The most recent `STATE->` transition in each interval, rendered as a state band.*

###### Reading it:
*Shows at a glance how long the node spent in each state and exactly when it left full.*

###### Healthy range:
*One unbroken full band across the window.*

###### Watch for:
*Any band that is not full, and repeated narrow bands, which indicate state flapping.*

###### Keywords:
- **Operating mode / server state** *(per node)* — the node's sync level: Disconnected, Connected, Syncing, Tracking, Full.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — one band per server per state.*
*NOT recorded as a metric anywhere. Derived in the Grafana query by regex over raw log text.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`NetworkOPsImp::setMode`

###### Note:
*Only transitions are logged, so a node that never changes state produces no data here. Read with the transition-rate panel beside it.*

###### References:
[Server states](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/rippled-server-states)

targets.expr: sum by (state, service_instance_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `STATE->(?P<state>\w+)` | state != `` | label_format state=`{{if eq .state "full"}}Full{{else if eq .state "syncing"}}Syncing{{else if eq .state "tracking"}}Tracking{{else if eq .state "connected"}}Connected{{else if eq .state "disconnected"}}Disconnected{{else}}{{.state}}{{end}}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Log Line Rate By Severity
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of log lines emitted by xrpld, split by severity.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of matching log lines grouped by the severity field parsed out of each line.*

###### Reading it:
*Use this to confirm the log pipeline is alive, and to see at a glance whether DBG lines are being collected at all.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent. If the DBG series is absent, every panel in a [DBG] row on this dashboard will be empty.*

###### Watch for:
*A sudden collapse to only WRN and ERR, which means debug logging was turned off and the [DBG] rows have gone blind rather than quiet.*

###### Keywords:
- **Severity** *(per line)* — xrpld log level: DBG, NFO, WRN, ERR, FTL.
- **Structured metadata** *(per line)* — Loki fields parsed from the line, filtered with `|` rather than in the stream selector.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per severity — a count of log lines, not of events in the node.*
*Derived in the Grafana query; the collector's filelog receiver parses severity, xrpld itself exports no such metric.*

###### Source:
[Log.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/basics/Log.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logs::Sink::write`

###### References:
[Loki structured metadata](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/get-started/labels/structured-metadata/)

targets.expr: sum by (severity, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity =~ "$severity" | label_format severity=`{{if eq .severity "DBG"}}Debug{{else if eq .severity "NFO"}}Info{{else if eq .severity "WRN"}}Warning{{else if eq .severity "ERR"}}Error{{else if eq .severity "FTL"}}Fatal{{else}}{{.severity}}{{end}}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Log Line Rate By Partition (Top $topn)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The busiest xrpld log partitions by line rate.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of log lines grouped by the partition field, limited to the top N series.*

###### Reading it:
*Shows which subsystem dominates log volume, which is the main cost driver for Loki ingest.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent. Resource, JobQueue, and LedgerConsensus are normally the loudest.*

###### Watch for:
*A partition suddenly dominating, which usually means a subsystem entered a retry or error loop.*

###### Keywords:
- **Partition** *(per line)* — the xrpld subsystem that emitted the line, e.g. ManifestCache, Resource, LedgerConsensus.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per partition — a count of log lines.*
*Derived in the Grafana query; truncated to the top N by Loki's series limit.*

###### Source:
[Log.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/basics/Log.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logs::Sink::write`

###### References:
[Loki log queries](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/log_queries/)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (partition, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity =~ "$severity" [$__auto])))

panels.title: Manifest Disposition Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of manifest apply outcomes: accepted, stale, revoked, invalid, or rate-limited.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of ManifestCache log lines, with the action parsed out of the `Manifest: <action>;Pk: ...` text.*

###### Reading it:
*AcceptedNew and AcceptedUpdate are useful work; Stale and UntrustedCapacity are rejections and normally dominate.*

###### Healthy range:
*Accepted rates are low and bursty. A high sustained Stale rate is normal — peers gossip manifests this node already holds.*

###### Watch for:
*Any Invalid, which means a signature failed verification, and a sustained UntrustedCapacity climb, which indicates a manifest flood from unlisted keys.*

###### Keywords:
- **Manifest** *(per validator)* — a signed record binding a validator's master key to its current signing key.
- **Disposition** *(per manifest)* — the apply outcome: AcceptedNew, AcceptedUpdate, Stale, Revoked, Invalid, UntrustedCapacity.
- **Stale** *(per manifest)* — sequence number not greater than the one already held; the common benign rejection.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per action — counts log EVENTS, not distinct manifests.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. `applyManifest` has no instrumentation; this is regex over `logMftAct` output in the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[Manifest.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/server/Manifest.cpp)

###### Function:
`ManifestCache::applyManifest / logMftAct`

###### References:
[Validator keys](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/validator-keys)

targets.expr: sum by (action, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `ManifestCache` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Manifest: (?P<action>[A-Za-z]+);` | action =~ "$manifest_action" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Manifest Accept Vs Reject Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Manifest outcomes collapsed into two series: accepted versus rejected.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second counts of ManifestCache lines, with AcceptedNew and AcceptedUpdate summed as accepted and all other actions summed as rejected.*

###### Reading it:
*Gives the useful-work fraction of inbound manifest processing without per-action detail.*

###### Healthy range:
*Rejected normally far exceeds accepted; peers routinely re-gossip known manifests.*

###### Watch for:
*A rejected rate in the hundreds per second, which indicates a manifest flood consuming the JtManifest job queue.*

###### Keywords:
- **Accepted** *(per manifest)* — AcceptedNew or AcceptedUpdate; the manifest changed cache state.
- **Rejected** *(per manifest)* — Stale, Invalid, Revoked, or UntrustedCapacity.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — two summed series over the same log lines.*
*Derived in the Grafana query. Accepted may legitimately be absent: measured 1,360 AcceptedNew per 7d, so short windows often contain none. Both series carry `or vector(0)` so a zero-accept window renders a flat zero line rather than disappearing.*

###### Source:
[Manifest.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/server/Manifest.cpp)

###### Function:
`ManifestCache::applyManifest / logMftAct`

###### References:
[Validator keys](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/validator-keys)

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `ManifestCache` | severity =~ "$severity" |~ `Manifest: Accepted` [$__auto])) or vector(0)

sum by (service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `ManifestCache` | severity =~ "$severity" |~ `Manifest: (Stale|Invalid|Revoked|UntrustedCapacity)` [$__auto])) or vector(0)

panels.title: Top $topn Manifest Producers By Master Key
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The master keys responsible for the most manifest log events in the selected window.*

###### How it's computed:
*Count of ManifestCache lines grouped by the base58 master key parsed from the log text, limited to the top N.
Counts are per log EVENT, not per distinct manifest.*

###### Reading it:
*Identifies which validator keys generate the most manifest churn on this node.*

###### Healthy range:
*A small number of keys with modest repeat counts. Live observation shows roughly 19 to 24 events per key per hour.*

###### Watch for:
*A single unlisted key with a very high count, which is the signature of a targeted manifest flood.*

###### Keywords:
- **Master key** *(per validator)* — the long-lived base58 key a manifest is signed under.
- **Log event** *(per line)* — one manifest apply attempt; the same key recurs as peers re-gossip.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per master key per node — counts log EVENTS, NOT distinct manifests and NOT distinct keys.*
*Derived in the Grafana query. Truncated to top N: Loki rejects queries returning over 2000 series, so a true distinct-key count is impossible here.*

###### Source:
[Manifest.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/server/Manifest.cpp)

###### Function:
`logMftAct`

###### Note:
*Truncated to the top N. Loki rejects a query returning over 2000 series, so a full distinct-key count is not possible here.*

###### References:
[Validator keys](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/validator-keys)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (pk, service_instance_id) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `ManifestCache` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Manifest: (?P<action>[A-Za-z]+);Pk: (?P<pk>[A-Za-z0-9]+);` | pk != `` | action =~ "$manifest_action" [$__range])))

panels.title: Fee Charge Rate By Reason
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate at which this node charges peers a resource fee, split by the reason for the charge.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of Resource log lines, with the reason parsed from the `for <reason> ($<fee>)` text.*

###### Reading it:
*Shows what kind of peer behaviour is costing this node the most. Moderate peer request normally dominates.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent and roughly proportional to peer count and request volume.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising useless data rate, which means peers are sending malformed or unwanted payloads.*

###### Keywords:
- **Resource fee** *(per peer)* — an internal load credit charged against a peer, unrelated to XRP transaction fees.
- **Reason** *(per charge)* — why the charge was applied, e.g. moderate peer request, useless data.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per reason — a count of charge events.*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query from `Logic::charge` log output.*

###### Source:
[ResourceManager.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/resource/detail/ResourceManager.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logic::charge`

###### References:
[Peer protocol](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/peer-protocol)

targets.expr: sum by (reason, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `Resource` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `for (?P<reason>[a-z ]+) \(\$(?P<fee>[0-9]+)\)` | reason =~ "$charge_reason" | reason != `` | label_format reason=`{{if eq .reason "useless data"}}Useless Data{{else if eq .reason "moderate peer request"}}Moderate Peer Request{{else if eq .reason "heavy peer request"}}Heavy Peer Request{{else if eq .reason "light peer request"}}Light Peer Request{{else if eq .reason "trivial peer request"}}Trivial Peer Request{{else if eq .reason "unwanted data"}}Unwanted Data{{else if eq .reason "init drop"}}Init Drop{{else}}{{.reason}}{{end}}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Fee-Weighted Charge Load
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Resource fee charges weighted by the fee amount, rather than counted equally.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second sum of the fee value parsed from each Resource charge line, using LogQL unwrap.*

###### Reading it:
*A single heavy peer request at 2000 outweighs eight moderate ones at 250, so this ranks real cost rather than event count.*

###### Healthy range:
*Workload-dependent; should track peer request volume smoothly.*

###### Watch for:
*Spikes that do not appear in the charge-count panel, which mean a shift toward expensive request types.*

###### Keywords:
- **Fee weight** *(per charge)* — the credit amount, e.g. 250 moderate, 2000 heavy; higher means costlier.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per reason — a SUM of fee amounts, not a count of events.*
*Derived in the Grafana query via LogQL `unwrap` over the parsed fee value.*

###### Source:
[ResourceManager.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/resource/detail/ResourceManager.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logic::charge`

###### References:
[Peer protocol](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/peer-protocol)

targets.expr: sum by (reason, service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `Resource` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `for (?P<reason>[a-z ]+) \(\$(?P<fee>[0-9]+)\)` | reason =~ "$charge_reason" | reason != `` | label_format reason=`{{if eq .reason "useless data"}}Useless Data{{else if eq .reason "moderate peer request"}}Moderate Peer Request{{else if eq .reason "heavy peer request"}}Heavy Peer Request{{else if eq .reason "light peer request"}}Light Peer Request{{else if eq .reason "trivial peer request"}}Trivial Peer Request{{else if eq .reason "unwanted data"}}Unwanted Data{{else if eq .reason "init drop"}}Init Drop{{else}}{{.reason}}{{end}}` | unwrap fee [$__auto]))

panels.title: Top $topn Charged Peers By IP And Public Key
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The peers accumulating the most resource fee charges, identified by IP address and node public key.*

###### How it's computed:
*Sum of fee amounts parsed from Resource charge lines, grouped by IP and public key, limited to the top N.*

###### Reading it:
*This is the direct answer to which peer is costing this node the most, and is the primary abuse-attribution view.*

###### Healthy range:
*Charges spread across many peers with no single dominant entry.*

###### Watch for:
*One IP far above the rest, especially paired with the useless data reason, which indicates an abusive or misbehaving peer.*

###### Keywords:
- **Node public key** *(per peer)* — the peer's base58 identity, stable across reconnects.
- **IP address** *(per peer)* — source address; the optional `:port` suffix is stripped so one peer is one row.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per peer per node — a SUM of fee amounts over the dashboard window.*
*Derived in the Grafana query. Truncated to top N by Loki's 2000-series limit, so this is the head of the distribution, never a total.*

###### Source:
[ResourceManager.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/resource/detail/ResourceManager.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logic::charge`

###### Note:
*Truncated to the top N because of Loki's 2000-series query limit.*

###### References:
[Peer protocol](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/peer-protocol)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (ip, pubkey, service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `Resource` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Charging IP Address: (?P<ip>[0-9a-fA-F:.]+?)(?::[0-9]+)?, Public Key: (?P<pubkey>[A-Za-z0-9]+) for (?P<reason>[a-z ]+) \(\$(?P<fee>[0-9]+)\)` | reason =~ "$charge_reason" | unwrap fee [$__range])))

panels.title: Ledger Node Fetch Duplicate Ratio
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The fraction of fetched ledger nodes that were duplicates this node already held.*

###### How it's computed:
*Sum of the dupe counter divided by the sum of good plus dupe, parsed from the `Ledger AS/TX node stats` log lines. Each field is matched independently because the emitter omits any counter that is zero.*

###### Reading it:
*This is wasted ledger-fetch bandwidth. A ratio of 0.5 means half of everything fetched was already present.*

###### Healthy range:
*Below roughly 0.3. Some duplication is unavoidable when fetching from several peers at once.*

###### Watch for:
*Sustained values above 0.8. Live observation has recorded good:142 dupe:891, an 86 percent duplicate rate, which wastes both bandwidth and peer resource credit.*

###### Keywords:
- **Ledger node** *(per fetch)* — one SHAMap node fetched while acquiring a ledger.
- **Duplicate** *(per fetch)* — a node already held locally; wasted bandwidth and peer credit.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — a ratio of two summed counters, dupe / (good + dupe).*
*NOT recorded as a metric. Derived in the Grafana query via `unwrap` over the counters in the InboundLedger stats line.*

###### Source:
[InboundLedger.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/ledger/detail/InboundLedger.cpp)

###### Function:
`InboundLedger::onTimer / takeAsRootNode`

###### References:
[Ledgers](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers)

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `InboundLedger` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `dupe:(?P<dupe>[0-9]+)` | unwrap dupe [$__auto])) / (sum by (service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `InboundLedger` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `dupe:(?P<dupe>[0-9]+)` | unwrap dupe [$__auto])) + sum by (service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `InboundLedger` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `good:(?P<good>[0-9]+)` | unwrap good [$__auto])))

panels.title: Ledger Node Fetch Rate — Good Vs Duplicate Vs Timeout
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Absolute rate of useful ledger nodes fetched, duplicates received, and acquire timeouts.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second sums of the good, dupe, and timeouts counters parsed from InboundLedger acquire log lines.*

###### Reading it:
*Gives the absolute volumes behind the duplicate-ratio panel, so a high ratio at trivial volume can be told apart from a high ratio at scale.*

###### Healthy range:
*Good should exceed duplicate during active sync. Timeouts should stay near zero.*

###### Watch for:
*A rising timeout series, which means peers are not answering ledger requests and sync will stall.*

###### Keywords:
- **Good** *(per fetch)* — a useful, previously unheld ledger node.
- **Timeout** *(per acquire)* — a ledger request a peer never answered.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — SUMS of the parsed counters, giving absolute volumes behind the ratio panel.*
*Derived in the Grafana query via `unwrap`.*

###### Source:
[InboundLedger.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/ledger/detail/InboundLedger.cpp)

###### Function:
`InboundLedger::onTimer`

###### References:
[Ledgers](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/ledgers)

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `InboundLedger` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `good:(?P<good>[0-9]+)` | unwrap good [$__auto]))

sum by (service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `InboundLedger` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `dupe:(?P<dupe>[0-9]+)` | unwrap dupe [$__auto]))

sum by (service_instance_id) (sum_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `InboundLedger` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Acquire \S+ timeouts:(?P<timeouts>[0-9]+)` | unwrap timeouts [$__auto]))

panels.title: Peer Disconnect Rate By Reason
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of peer connection endings, split by the reason recorded in the log.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of Peer log lines matching Timeout, Closed, or a refused connection attempt.*

###### Reading it:
*Distinguishes clean teardown from failure. Closed is a normal ending; Timeout and Connection refused are not.*

###### Healthy range:
*Closed dominant with a low, steady background of the others.*

###### Watch for:
*A Timeout rate approaching the Closed rate, which points at network trouble or unresponsive peers.*

###### Keywords:
- **Closed** *(per peer)* — a clean connection teardown; the normal ending.
- **Timeout** *(per peer)* — the peer stopped responding.
- **Connection refused** *(per attempt)* — an outbound attempt the remote rejected.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per outcome — a count of peer lifecycle events.*
*Derived in the Grafana query. Note `overlay_peer_disconnects` exists as a metric but carries no reason breakdown, which is what this panel adds.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::close / onTimer`

###### References:
[Peer protocol](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/peer-protocol)

targets.expr: sum by (outcome, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `Peer` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `\] (?P<outcome>Timeout|Closed|onConnect: Connection refused)` | outcome != `` | label_format outcome=`{{if eq .outcome "Closed"}}Closed{{else if eq .outcome "Timeout"}}Timeout{{else if eq .outcome "onConnect: Connection refused"}}Connection Refused{{else}}{{.outcome}}{{end}}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Peer Handshake And Accept Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of completed peer handshakes and accepted inbound connections.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of PeerFinder log lines matching handshake and accept events.*

###### Reading it:
*Read together with the disconnect panel: healthy churn has handshakes roughly balancing disconnects.*

###### Healthy range:
*Low and steady once the node has a full peer slate.*

###### Watch for:
*A high handshake rate alongside a high disconnect rate, which means peers connect and immediately drop.*

###### Keywords:
- **Handshake** *(per peer)* — protocol negotiation completed with a peer.
- **Accept** *(per peer)* — an inbound connection admitted to a peer slot.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — counts of PeerFinder events.*
*Derived in the Grafana query.*

###### Source:
[Logic.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/peerfinder/detail/Logic.h)

###### Function:
`Logic::on_handshake / on_accept`

###### References:
[Peer protocol](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/networks-and-servers/peer-protocol)

targets.expr: sum by (service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `PeerFinder` | severity =~ "$severity" |~ `Logic handshake` [$__auto]))

sum by (service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `PeerFinder` | severity =~ "$severity" |~ `Logic accept` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Consensus Phase Transition Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of consensus phase transitions into Open, Establish, and Accepted.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of log lines announcing a ConsensusPhase transition, grouped by the target phase.*

###### Reading it:
*A healthy node cycles Open to Establish to Accepted once per ledger, so all three series should track together.*

###### Healthy range:
*Roughly one transition per phase per ledger interval, near 0.25 per second on a 4-second close.*

###### Watch for:
*Establish transitions outnumbering Accepted, which means rounds start but fail to converge.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus phase** *(per round)* — Open collects transactions, Establish converges on a set, Accepted applies it.
- **Transition** *(per round)* — one phase change; a healthy node cycles all three once per ledger.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per phase — a count of transitions.*
*Derived in the Grafana query by regex over the phase-change log line.*

###### Source:
[Consensus.h](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/include/xrpl/consensus/Consensus.h)

###### Function:
`Consensus::phase transition logging`

###### References:
[Consensus](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol)

targets.expr: sum by (phase, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `[Tt]ransitioned to ConsensusPhase::(?P<phase>\w+)` | phase =~ "$consensus_phase" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Consensus Operating Mode Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of consensus heartbeat log lines, split by the operating mode reported in each.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of ConsensusLogger heartbeat lines, with the mode parsed from the `mode: <value>` text.*

###### Reading it:
*This acts as a mode-occupancy proxy: the heartbeat fires about once per second, so the dominant series is the node's current mode.*

###### Healthy range:
*Almost entirely the full series on a synced node.*

###### Watch for:
*Any sustained syncing, observing, or tracking share, which means the node is not participating normally.*

###### Keywords:
- **Consensus mode** *(per node)* — the node's participation level: full proposing, observing, syncing, tracking.
- **Heartbeat** *(per second)* — the ConsensusLogger timer line, emitted roughly once per second.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per mode — a count of heartbeat lines, used as a mode-occupancy PROXY rather than a true duration.*
*Derived in the Grafana query. For exact durations use the state_accounting metrics on the Node Health dashboard.*

###### Source:
[NetworkOPs.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/NetworkOPs.cpp)

###### Function:
`ConsensusLogger heartbeat`

###### References:
[Consensus](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol)

targets.expr: sum by (mode, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `NetworkOPs` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `ConsensusLogger.*?mode: (?P<mode>\w+)\.` | mode =~ "$consensus_mode" | mode != `` | label_format mode=`{{if eq .mode "full"}}Full{{else if eq .mode "syncing"}}Syncing{{else if eq .mode "observing"}}Observing{{else if eq .mode "tracking"}}Tracking{{else}}{{.mode}}{{end}}` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Validator List Quorum And Trusted Set Size
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The quorum threshold and trusted validator count this node computed, as recorded in the log.*

###### How it's computed:
*Quorum and total are parsed from the `Using quorum of N for new set of M trusted validators` line and plotted as values.*

###### Reading it:
*Confirms the node agrees with the network on how many validators it trusts and how many must agree.*

###### Healthy range:
*Stable, with quorum at roughly 80 percent of the trusted total.*

###### Watch for:
*A drop in the trusted total, which shrinks the quorum and weakens the node's safety margin.*

###### Keywords:
- **Quorum** *(per node)* — how many trusted validators must agree; normally about 80 percent of the trusted set.
- **Trusted set** *(per node)* — validators from the UNL this node currently trusts.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — the last VALUE parsed from the log line, not a rate or count.*
*Derived in the Grafana query via `unwrap`. Overlaps the `unl_quorum` metric; prefer that metric for the value and this panel for churn events.*

###### Source:
[ValidatorList.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/app/misc/detail/ValidatorList.cpp)

###### Function:
`ValidatorList::updateTrusted`

###### References:
[Unique Node List](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol/unique-node-list)

targets.expr: max by (service_instance_id) (max_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `ValidatorList` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Using quorum of (?P<quorum>[0-9]+) for new set of (?P<total>[0-9]+) trusted` | unwrap quorum [$__auto]))

max by (service_instance_id) (max_over_time({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `ValidatorList` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Using quorum of (?P<quorum>[0-9]+) for new set of (?P<total>[0-9]+) trusted` | unwrap total [$__auto]))

panels.title: Slow Job Run Time (p99)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 99th percentile run time of jobs that breached their latency target.*

###### How it's computed:
*Quantile over the run millisecond value parsed from LoadMonitor job lines, grouped by job name.*

###### Reading it:
*Identifies which job types are the slowest when they do run long.*

###### Healthy range:
*Only a handful of job names should appear at all. Values in the tens of seconds indicate real stalls.*

###### Watch for:
*ProcessLData or InboundLedger dominating, which is the signature of the cold-read sync bottleneck.*

###### Keywords:
- **Job** *(per task)* — a unit of work on xrpld's job queue, e.g. ProcessLData, InboundLedger.
- **Run time** *(per job)* — time spent executing, excluding queue wait.
- **Breach** *(per job)* — an execution exceeding the 500ms LoadMonitor threshold; only these are logged.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per job type — a p99 over BREACHES ONLY, never over all executions.*
*Derived in the Grafana query via `unwrap`. For total job counts and latencies use the native `job_*` metrics on the Job Queue Analysis dashboard.*

###### Source:
[LoadMonitor.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/LoadMonitor.cpp)

###### Function:
`LoadMonitor::addLoadSample`

###### Note:
*These lines are only emitted above a 500ms latency threshold, so this panel counts BREACHES, never total job executions. Use the Job Queue Analysis dashboard for totals.*

###### References:
[Job queue](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/JobQueue.cpp)

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.99, {service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `LoadMonitor` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Job: (?P<jobname>\S+) run: (?P<run>[0-9]+)ms wait: (?P<wait>[0-9]+)ms` | unwrap run [$__auto]) by (jobname, service_instance_id)

panels.title: Slow Job Breach Rate By Job Name (Top $topn)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How often each job type breaches its latency target.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of LoadMonitor job lines grouped by job name, limited to the top N.*

###### Reading it:
*Read with the p99 panel: a job can breach rarely but severely, or often but mildly.*

###### Healthy range:
*Near zero. Any sustained non-zero rate means a job type is routinely missing its target.*

###### Watch for:
*A step change after a deploy, which points at a regression in that job's path.*

###### Keywords:
- **Breach** *(per job)* — an execution over the 500ms threshold.
- **Job type** *(per task)* — the named job class, e.g. sweep, ProcessLData.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per job type — a count of BREACHES, not of executions.*
*Derived in the Grafana query; truncated to top N.*

###### Source:
[LoadMonitor.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/LoadMonitor.cpp)

###### Function:
`LoadMonitor::addLoadSample`

###### Note:
*Counts BREACHES above the 500ms threshold, not total job executions.*

###### References:
[Job queue](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/JobQueue.cpp)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (jobname, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `LoadMonitor` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Job: (?P<jobname>\S+) run: (?P<run>[0-9]+)ms wait: (?P<wait>[0-9]+)ms` | jobname != `` [$__auto])))

panels.title: Slow Job Queue Wait Time (p99)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The 99th percentile queue wait time of jobs that breached their latency target.*

###### How it's computed:
*Quantile over the wait millisecond value parsed from LoadMonitor job lines, grouped by job name.*

###### Reading it:
*Separates queueing delay from execution cost. High wait with low run means the job queue is saturated rather than the work being slow.*

###### Healthy range:
*Near zero. Live observation shows wait at 0ms for most breaches, meaning run time is the cause.*

###### Watch for:
*Wait time rising above run time, which shifts the diagnosis from slow work to a saturated job queue.*

###### Keywords:
- **Wait time** *(per job)* — time queued before execution began.
- **Run versus wait** *(per job)* — high wait means a saturated queue; high run means slow work.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per job type — a p99 over BREACHES ONLY.*
*Derived in the Grafana query via `unwrap`.*

###### Source:
[LoadMonitor.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/LoadMonitor.cpp)

###### Function:
`LoadMonitor::addLoadSample`

###### Note:
*Counts BREACHES above the 500ms threshold, not total job executions.*

###### References:
[Job queue](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/core/detail/JobQueue.cpp)

targets.expr: quantile_over_time(0.99, {service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | partition = `LoadMonitor` | severity =~ "$severity" | regexp `Job: (?P<jobname>\S+) run: (?P<run>[0-9]+)ms wait: (?P<wait>[0-9]+)ms` | unwrap wait [$__auto]) by (jobname, service_instance_id)

panels.title: Warning And Error Rate By Partition (Top $topn)
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Rate of WRN, ERR, and FTL log lines by partition.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-second count of log lines at warning severity or above, grouped by partition and limited to the top N.*

###### Reading it:
*This is the one row that works fully at default log level, so it is the first place to look on an unmodified node.*

###### Healthy range:
*Low and flat. LoadMonitor warnings are expected on a busy node.*

###### Watch for:
*Any ERR or FTL series appearing, and step changes in a partition that is normally quiet.*

###### Keywords:
- **Severity** *(per line)* — WRN, ERR, or FTL; the levels a default-configured node still writes.
- **Partition** *(per line)* — the emitting xrpld subsystem.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node per partition per severity — a count of log lines.*
*Derived in the Grafana query. This row is the only one that works fully at default log level.*

###### Source:
[Log.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/basics/Log.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logs::Sink::write`

###### References:
[Loki log queries](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/log_queries/)

targets.expr: topk($topn, sum by (partition, severity, service_instance_id) (rate({service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity =~ `WRN|ERR|FTL` [$__auto])))

panels.title: Recent Warnings And Errors
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The most recent log lines at warning severity or above.*

###### How it's computed:
*Raw log stream filtered to WRN, ERR, and FTL, newest first.*

###### Reading it:
*Use this to read the actual text behind a spike in the rate panel beside it.*

###### Healthy range:
*Sparse. LoadMonitor slow-job warnings are the common benign entry.*

###### Watch for:
*Repeating identical errors, which indicate a stuck retry loop rather than a transient fault.*

###### Keywords:
- **Log stream** *(per node)* — the raw lines behind the aggregate rates, newest first.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Raw log lines, no aggregation.*
*Rendered directly from Loki; no computation applied.*

###### Source:
[Log.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/basics/Log.cpp)

###### Function:
`Logs::Sink::write`

###### References:
[Loki log queries](https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/query/log_queries/)

targets.expr: {service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity =~ `WRN|ERR|FTL` | line_format `{{.partition}}:{{.severity}} {{.message}}`
